newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tax authorities raid Murdoch Israel subsidiary.
newsitem.headline: Tax authorities raid Murdoch Israel subsidiary.

text.p: Israeli tax authorities said on Sunday they had raided the offices of a company controlled by media magnate Rupert Murdoch and removed documents.
News Datacom Research Ltd, a Jerusalem-based company controlled by Murdoch's UK-based News Corp, forcefully denied any wrongdoing.
"We are directing an investigation against News Datacom Research," said Sarit Giladi-Dor, a spokeswoman for the Income Tax Authority.

"The company is suspected of concealing income in the years 1989-1996 of some 150 million dollars," the tax authority said in a statement. The statement said the authority had been investigating News Datacom undercover for the past year and was launching an open investigation.
The statement said investigators had also raided the offices of News Datacom's attorneys and auditors, including the law firm Herzog Fox Ne'eman, one of Israel's most prestigious.
The statement said no arrests had been made in the case and that the authority had not issued a petition to detain Murdoch, contrary to Israeli media reports.
News Datacom said it was "appalled" by the allegations.
"Allegations of tax evasion are entirely without merit," the company said in an unsigned statement.
"The company also wishes to clarify that it has not received any research grants which carry any restrictions on technology transfer - contrary to some media reports."
News Datacom develops and sells encryption systems mainly for pay television broadcasters, like Murdoch's SKY Television.

The News Datacom statement attributed leaks to the media about the investigation to "a continuing extortion campaign against the company by former employees who have been sued in the UK by NDC (the Israeli company's parent) for defrauding it of millions of dollars," it said.
